options: Downloads changes without touching your branch
Fetches from the tracked remote branch and puts your local commits on top of the remote ones
Pushes your commits and rebases the remote
questions.explanation: It is equivalent to `git fetch` followed by `git rebase`: your local commits are replayed on top of the fetched ones.

questions.prompt: In a fork-based setup, what do `origin` and `upstream` usually point to?
questions.explanation: The typical setup: `origin` → your fork, `upstream` → the original repository.

questions.prompt: Which command connects a local repository to a remote for the first time?
questions.explanation: `git remote add origin <url>` connects the local repo to a remote; `git remote -v` lists the remotes you have.
